condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: The query is 2,4-diamino-5-(3,4,5-trimethoxybenzyl)pyrimidine; the closest transferable contexts sharing the trimethoxybenzyl/trimethoxyphenyl motif report absolute oral bioavailability values well above 20%: trimetazidine 88.7% (reported range 30-90%), fostamatinib 54.6%, rigosertib 34.8-35%, and colchicine means of 37-47% (range 24-88%).

L2 records from these close contexts reinforce the direction: fostamatinib is described as ~55% bioavailable and highly bioavailable after oral dosing; trimetazidine formulations show enhanced relative bioavailability; rigosertib fasting F is 35±18% and adequate/predictable; colchicine absolute F is repeatedly ~44-45%; etoposide phosphate oral F is 68-76%.

No transferable affirmative evidence supports F<20% for the query. The only sub-20 values are rat isoeugenol records (10-19%) from a structurally distant phenol context, and the human isoeugenol L1 value is 35.8-39.0%; these do not transfer to the trimethoxybenzyl diaminopyrimidine.
Additional less-similar contexts also report F above 20%: acitretin ~40-60% (105% in one study), etoposide ~50%, etoposide phosphate 68%, estragole 32%, and isoeugenol 35.8-39%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule was supplied; the decision is based on transfer from structurally related contexts and a physicochemical prior.
No query-specific data on first-pass metabolism, efflux transport, or formulation-dependent absorption were supplied.
Some supporting records are model predictions or estimates (e.g., C24, C28, C19) rather than measured absolute bioavailability, but their values still exceed 20%.
The low rat isoeugenol values (C39, C41, C44, C76) are species-specific and from a structurally distant context; their transferability to the query is low.
C58 indicates that a closely related parent (R406) has poor solubility, but the query has a favorable solubility prior and no query-specific dissolution data were supplied.
